stem: If the sum of two unit vectors is a unit vector, then the magnitude of their difference is:
solution: For unit vectors with \(|\vec a+\vec b|=1\): \(1=1+1+2\cos\theta\Rightarrow\cos\theta=-1/2\). Then \(|\vec a-\vec b|^2=1+1-2\cos\theta=3\), so \(|\vec a-\vec b|=\sqrt{3}\). Matches option C.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: A vector \(\vec A\) points vertically upwards and \(\vec B\) points towards the north. The vector product \(\vec A\times\vec B\) is along:
solution: Take East \(=\hat i\), North \(=\hat j\), Up \(=\hat k\). Then \(\vec A=\hat k,\ \vec B=\hat j\) and \(\hat k\times\hat j=-\hat i\), i.e. towards the West. Matches option A.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: The angle between the vectors \((\hat i+\hat j)\) and \((\hat j+\hat k)\) is:
solution: \(\cos\theta=\dfrac{(\hat i+\hat j)\cdot(\hat j+\hat k)}{\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt2}=\dfrac{1}{2}\), so \(\theta=60^\circ\). Matches option C.

stem: The components of a vector along the x and y axes are 2 units and 3 units respectively. If the coordinate axes are rotated through an angle of \(45^\circ\) counter-clockwise, the magnitude of the vector in the new system will be:
solution: The magnitude of a vector is invariant under a rotation of the coordinate axes: \(\sqrt{2^2+3^2}=\sqrt{13}\). Matches option A.

stem: Three vectors \(\vec P,\ \vec Q\) and \(\vec R\) satisfy the equation \(\vec P+\vec Q=\vec R\) and their magnitudes are related by \(P^2+Q^2=R^2\). The angle between \(\vec P\) and \(\vec Q\) is:
solution: \(R^2=P^2+Q^2+2PQ\cos\theta\). Given \(R^2=P^2+Q^2\Rightarrow\cos\theta=0\Rightarrow\theta=\pi/2\). Matches option C.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: A particle moves from position \((2\hat i+3\hat j-\hat k)\) m to \((4\hat i+6\hat j-3\hat k)\) m under the action of a constant force \(\vec F=(3\hat i+2\hat j+4\hat k)\) N. The work done by the force is:
solution: Displacement \(\vec d=(2\hat i+3\hat j-2\hat k)\) m. \(W=\vec F\cdot\vec d=6+6-8=4\) J. Matches option A.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: What is the unit vector perpendicular to both \(\vec A=2\hat i+3\hat j+\hat k\) and \(\vec B=\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k\)?
solution: \(\vec A\times\vec B=(7\hat i-3\hat j-5\hat k)\), with \(|\vec A\times\vec B|=\sqrt{83}\). The perpendicular unit vector is \((7\hat i-3\hat j-5\hat k)/\sqrt{83}\). Matches option A.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: The area of the parallelogram whose diagonals are represented by the vectors \(\vec A=3\hat i+\hat j-2\hat k\) and \(\vec B=\hat i-3\hat j+4\hat k\) is:
solution: Area \(=\tfrac12|\vec A\times\vec B|\). \(\vec A\times\vec B=(-2\hat i-14\hat j-10\hat k)\), \(|\vec A\times\vec B|=\sqrt{300}=10\sqrt3\), so the area \(=5\sqrt3\ (=\sqrt{75})\) units. This value is NOT among the printed options; option B (\(\sqrt{42}\)) is keyed only as the nearest choice for OMR grading.
reviewNote: FLAWED: correct answer 5√3 = √75 ≈ 8.66 is not among the options (√21, √42, 2√42, 4√2). Official LWS key = B; keyed B to match (still a defective question — no option is exactly correct).

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: If \(|\vec A\times\vec B|=\sqrt3\,(\vec A\cdot\vec B)\), then the value of \(|\vec A+\vec B|\) is:
solution: \(AB\sin\theta=\sqrt3\,AB\cos\theta\Rightarrow\tan\theta=\sqrt3\Rightarrow\theta=60^\circ\). Then \(|\vec A+\vec B|^2=A^2+B^2+2AB\cos60^\circ=A^2+B^2+AB\). Matches option A.

stem: Which of the following physical quantities is a scalar quantity?
solution: Displacement, acceleration and force are vectors. Electric current has an associated direction but does not add as a vector (currents at a junction add algebraically), so it is treated as a scalar. Matches option B.

stem: The maximum and minimum magnitudes of the resultant of two vectors are 17 units and 7 units respectively. If these two vectors are perpendicular to each other, the magnitude of their resultant will be:
solution: \(A+B=17\) and \(A-B=7\Rightarrow A=12,\ B=5\). When perpendicular, resultant \(=\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=\sqrt{169}=13\). Matches option C.

stem: A vector \(\vec A\) when added to \(\vec B\) gives a resultant vector along the positive x-axis. When \(\vec A\) is subtracted from \(\vec B\), the resultant is along the negative y-axis. Which of the following orientations is correct?
optA: \(\vec A\) is in the 1st quadrant, \(\vec B\) is in the 3rd
optB: Both \(\vec A\) and \(\vec B\) are in the 1st quadrant
optC: \(\vec A\) is in the 4th quadrant, \(\vec B\) is in the 1st quadrant
optD: \(\vec A\) is in the 1st quadrant, \(\vec B\) is in the 4th quadrant
solution: Let \(\vec A+\vec B=(p,0)\) (along \(+x\)) and \(\vec B-\vec A=(0,-q)\) (along \(-y\)), with \(p,q>0\). Adding gives \(2\vec B=(p,-q)\Rightarrow\vec B=(p/2,-q/2)\) (4th quadrant); subtracting gives \(2\vec A=(p,q)\Rightarrow\vec A=(p/2,q/2)\) (1st quadrant). So \(\vec A\) is in the 1st quadrant and \(\vec B\) in the 4th. Matches option D.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: If three non-coplanar vectors \(\vec A,\ \vec B\) and \(\vec C\) satisfy \(\vec A\cdot(\vec B\times\vec C)=0\), then:
optB: The statement is false since non-coplanar scalar triple products cannot be zero
optC: Two of the vectors must be parallel
solution: A zero scalar triple product means the three vectors are coplanar, which contradicts the premise 'non-coplanar'. For genuinely non-coplanar vectors \(\vec A\cdot(\vec B\times\vec C)\neq0\). Matches option B.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: What is the angle between a vector \(\vec A\) and its negative vector \((-\vec A)\)?
solution: A vector and its negative point in exactly opposite directions, so the angle between them is \(180^\circ\). Matches option C.

stem: If a vector makes equal angles with the coordinate axes OX, OY and OZ, then the value of its direction cosines are:
solution: For equal angles \(l=m=n\), and \(l^2+m^2+n^2=1\Rightarrow3l^2=1\Rightarrow l=\pm1/\sqrt3\). Matches option C.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: The vector projection of \(\vec A=\hat i+3\hat j+\hat k\) on \(\vec B=2\hat i-3\hat j+6\hat k\) is:
solution: Vector projection \(=\dfrac{\vec A\cdot\vec B}{|\vec B|^2}\vec B\). Here \(\vec A\cdot\vec B=2-9+6=-1\) and \(|\vec B|^2=4+9+36=49\), giving \(-\tfrac{1}{49}(2\hat i-3\hat j+6\hat k)\). Matches option C.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: If \(\vec A,\ \vec B\) and \(\vec C\) are three vectors such that \(\vec A\cdot\vec B=\vec A\cdot\vec C\) and \(\vec A\times\vec B=\vec A\times\vec C\), and \(\vec A\) is not a null vector, then:
optD: \(\vec A\) is perpendicular to \((\vec B-\vec C)\)
solution: \(\vec A\cdot(\vec B-\vec C)=0\) makes \(\vec B-\vec C\perp\vec A\), while \(\vec A\times(\vec B-\vec C)=0\) makes it parallel to \(\vec A\). Both can hold only if \(\vec B-\vec C=\vec 0\), i.e. \(\vec B=\vec C\). Matches option B.

stem: The magnitude of a unit vector is always equal to:
solution: By definition a unit vector has magnitude 1. Matches option B.

stem: For any two vectors \(\vec A\) and \(\vec B\), the expression \(|\vec A+\vec B|^2+|\vec A-\vec B|^2\) is identically equal to:
solution: Expanding both squares, the cross terms cancel: \(|\vec A+\vec B|^2+|\vec A-\vec B|^2=2A^2+2B^2=2(A^2+B^2)\) (parallelogram law). Matches option A.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: A force \(\vec F=(2\hat i-\hat j-\hat k)\) N acts at a point \(P(1,-1,2)\) relative to the origin. The torque of this force about the origin is given by:
solution: \(\vec\tau=\vec r\times\vec F\) with \(\vec r=(1,-1,2),\ \vec F=(2,-1,-1)\), giving \(\vec\tau=(3\hat i+5\hat j+\hat k)\) N·m. Matches option A.

stem: A person walks 10 m North, then 20 m East, and finally \(20\sqrt2\) m Southwest. Find the net displacement from the initial starting point.
solution: Take East \(=\hat i\), North \(=\hat j\). Positions: \((0,10)\to(20,10)\); the \(20\sqrt2\) m Southwest step is \((-20,-20)\), ending at \((0,-10)\). Net displacement \(=10\) m due South. Matches option B.

subtopic: Dot Product, Cross Product and Angle
stem: If the angle between vectors \(\vec A\) and \(\vec B\) is \(\theta\), then the value of the scalar triple product \(\vec A\cdot(\vec B\times\vec A)\) is:
solution: \(\vec B\times\vec A\) is perpendicular to \(\vec A\), so \(\vec A\cdot(\vec B\times\vec A)=0\) (a scalar triple product with a repeated vector vanishes). Matches option C.

stem: A particle possesses a velocity of 5 m/s towards the east. In 10 seconds, its velocity changes to 5 m/s towards the north. The average acceleration of the particle during this time interval is:
solution: \(\Delta\vec v=\vec v_f-\vec v_i=5\,(\text{North})-5\,(\text{East})\), magnitude \(5\sqrt2\) m/s directed North-West. \(a_{avg}=\dfrac{5\sqrt2}{10}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\) m/s\(^2\) towards North-West. Matches option A.

stem: If vector \(\vec P\) makes an angle \(\alpha\) with the x-axis, \(\beta\) with the y-axis and \(\gamma\) with the z-axis, then the value of \(\sin^2\alpha+\sin^2\beta+\sin^2\gamma\) is equal to:
solution: Since \(\cos^2\alpha+\cos^2\beta+\cos^2\gamma=1\), we get \(\sin^2\alpha+\sin^2\beta+\sin^2\gamma=3-1=2\). Matches option B.

stem: The resultant of two forces acting at an angle \(\theta\) is \(R\). If one of the forces is reversed in direction, the resultant becomes \(S\). The value of \(R^2+S^2\) is:
solution: \(R^2=F_1^2+F_2^2+2F_1F_2\cos\theta\); reversing one force flips the sign, giving \(S^2=F_1^2+F_2^2-2F_1F_2\cos\theta\). Adding, \(R^2+S^2=2(F_1^2+F_2^2)\). Matches option A.
